response: Yes, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) is associated with carotid atherosclerosis in healthy Koreans. Elevated levels of hs-CRP have been linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, including carotid atherosclerosis, which is a condition characterized by the buildup of plaque in the carotid arteries. Studies have shown that hs-CRP is a useful biomarker for predicting cardiovascular risk, and its association with carotid atherosclerosis has been observed in various populations, including healthy Koreans.
